text: Like propositional logic, first-order logic is decidable: there is an algorithm that decides, for any sentence, whether it is valid.
explanation: False. By the Church–Turing result (1936), first-order validity is undecidable. FOL is only SEMI-decidable: a valid sentence will eventually be recognized, but the procedure may run forever on non-valid ones. Propositional logic is decidable, but FOL is not.
